_about: Chapter R (Resolve) of the suite results document, round 4 (after OWNER-REVIEW-SAMPLE-1.md and the re-verification of round 3): the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 for manifest v4 (units as in units_v4.json). `summary` (what held, and the timing in one paragraph) and `coverage_gap` (which claim remains unsupported) are printed first on the chapter page, before and after the summary block (standing, outcomes, agreement, timing, load, detail blocks); `intro` follows: the shortened /resolve background. `families` keys on the family id (the scenario id prefix) with a title, one paragraph of prose and a `claim` (the property in words; the generator sorts the claims into what the direct arms showed, over `claim_members` when the claim rests on some members only); `units` keys on the unit id with its one-line property, a string or {property, note} (the note printed in italics under the property line); `mcp_notes.units` keys on a unit id whose MCP column is wholly not exercised: the one line printed under its table (the per-case reasons are in cases.json); `coverage_gap_families` names the families whose footnoted tests the coverage gap discusses itself (the generator lists the others under {footnoted_elsewhere_text}). Keys are family and unit ids, never scenario ids. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*. EVERY FIGURE OF THE RUN IS A PLACEHOLDER the generator fills from the record (doc/facts.py), and every sentence whose truth depends on the run is a conditional `[[flag ? when true | when false]]`, so that a later run's document never prints this run's numbers: the chapter prose reads facts.chapter_facts (counts by standing and by agreement, the summary's timing figures, the findings, the claims held and unsupported, the footnoted tests, the gate; `fam[<family>][...]` a family's values; `x[<scenario>][dl|dr|mcp][wall|phrase|detail|class|...]` a scenario's), a family's prose facts.family_facts (its `n_tests`, `n_units`, the standing counts, the MCP classes as the cells derive them: `n_mcp_<class>`, `mcp_<class>_ids`, `mcp_<class>_variants`; the footnoted members' phrases, the findings, the late 503s, the stated stops, the relations, the declared exemptions, `x` over its members); `{n:s}` is the plural s, `{n:v}` the verb's s, `{n:word}` the number in words. The literal numbers that remain are the constants of the SPEC, of the manifest v4 (lengths, budgets, expected runs) and of the service, each listed under `_assumes` with its source; tests/test_doc.py fails on any other number. Every claim follows SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md section 4, areas.py gen_R, checks.py and service_by_design.json as of c11db9dd. The check catalogue is in checks.json, the glossary in glossary.json. Round 5 (after OWNER-REVIEW-SAMPLE-2.md): a timing sentence states no cause (latency varies across records; the controls do not isolate the length), the host state of a cell named in the prose comes from the record (`host_word`), an agreement's depth is stated over the repeats compared (`n_mcp_full_fewer_repeats`), the R-budget prose names its footnoted members once (the gap and the detail blocks hold the evidence) and every sentence that asserted the run (every call refused at submit, the twins' answers the same, the source outranked) is a conditional on a computed fact. The final patch (VERIFY-R4, issue 3): the number of a count's verb and noun follows the count ('is a finding' / 'are findings', 'the only test' / 'one of the two tests'). The v5 prose round (2026-10-15, after the v5 unit mapping doc/units/suite_v5.json): the file is written for the union of the v4 mapping (10 families, 14 units) and the v5 mapping (11 families, 15 units; R-warm, the warm-ups, is v5-only, and R-edge-0025 joins R-edge-accepted). title: Resolve
purpose: /resolve answers the first question a user asks of an index: does it know this sequence, and under which records? For each k-mer of a supplied sequence it reports which labels (a taxid column, an accession.version header) carry it, as runs over the query. That is label support, k-mer by k-mer: some sequence of the label holds each k-mer. It is not by itself evidence that the whole query occurs contiguously at one place of one record; only trace support approaches that (the Background says where the two part). This chapter's evidence is of the first kind of I.2's ground truth: windows cut from known records must resolve fully under their own labels, junctions must end where the records say, a refusal must carry the host's exact text, and a time budget must end the work as the contract states; what the MCP tools cannot express is said so, and a count of tests passing never includes a cell the tools could not exercise. The evidence map after the headline lists what each family claims and what the direct access paths showed of it; the exception index and the detail blocks hold the exceptions.

intro: POST /resolve maps a query to the labels that carry it (SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 4). For a query of L bases the host maps its L - k + 1 k-mers to the graph (on this basic graph the forward strand only) and reports `graph_runs`, the maximal runs of consecutive in-graph k-mers as 0-based half-open intervals of k-mer starts, and per requested label the k-mers it supports, as runs of the same form and as a count, `kmers_supported`. A column label (a taxid) supports an in-graph k-mer whose annotation row carries it; a header label (an accession.version) one at which some coordinate of its column maps to that sequence, and with support trace only while consecutive supported k-mers have consecutive coordinates (section 4.2). In plain terms: a label that supports every k-mer of the query says that each k-mer is carried by some sequence of that label, k-mer by k-mer (label support, I.1); it does not by itself show that the whole query occurs contiguously at one place of one record, since a taxid column gathers every record of the taxon, and even one header's supported k-mers may lie at different places of its sequence. Trace support adds the missing condition, consecutive coordinates in one sequence, and is this chapter's only evidence of a contiguous occurrence (R-trace); a full resolve without trace is evidence of support, no more. A taxid column is one column of the annotation with one or many records; a header is one record of a column, reached through its coordinates. Runs count k-mer starts, not bases: a 100 bp query at k = 31 has 70 k-mer starts, so the run [0, 70) is full coverage of the query and spans its bases [0, 100); every interval of this chapter is such a k-mer-start interval (the junctions' expected runs lie within the 170 k-mers of a 200 bp junction), whereas the coordinates chapter T reads with trace support (T-coords) are positions in the source record's bases. A request names exactly one of labels or discover; a discovery collects the labels of every in-graph k-mer's row, ranks them by supported k-mers, keeps the top `max_labels` (ties by column id, then sequence id) and states `labels_truncated` when it dropped some. Validation is strict: an unknown field, a wrong type, a value out of range, both or neither of labels and discover, a duplicate or unknown label, a query shorter than k or longer than the server's or the request's `max_query_bp` are 400s naming the problem. The select block (section 4.3) is not exercised by this chapter.

The time budget (section 4.5) is opt-in: `bounds.time_budget_ms`, above the finalisation reserve of 250 ms, lowered to the server's cap (60,000 ms on staging) and stated in limits.clamped when lowered. The work reads the deadline between its row batches and its pieces of k-mers and stops at the budget less the reserve; a stop answers, with status 200, exactly the resolve of a prefix of the query with a stop block (phase, reason time, `resolved_kmers`, `query_kmers`, `resolved_bp`, `remainder_from_bp`), so that a client resolves the rest from `remainder_from_bp`. Past the budget the answer is a 503 with the code deadline, never a partial answer. The pieces the deadline does not poll (the request's parse, the mapping of the query's k-mers, one row batch's decode, the explicit labels' resolution) can push a stop or a 503 past the budget; a 503 deadline is allowed, and inconclusive, wherever the request names a budget, and a finding only beyond max(1 s, the budget) (appendix A, `budget_respected`, whose decision table gives the cases; the lateness is read on the client's clock and its cause is not isolated). This is /resolve's rule alone: a /traverse budget is read per seed on the seed's own clock from depth 1 (chapter T's Background; I.2's budget table gives the scope per route).

Ground truth. The windows are cut from the records of I.2; the record's taxid column and its accession.version are the labels, and every k-mer of a window cut from the record is in the graph and supported by both. Lengths run from k to 2,000 bp, the cap the service sends on every explicit-label resolve; [[manifest_version = 5 ? the stops of R-budget, 5,000 and 10,000 bp, and their twins run up to the server's limit of 10,000 bp and reach the host on the direct access paths only. R-pos, R-multi, R-junction, R-trace, R-rc, R-order, R-twin-case, R-warm and most of R-edge name `bounds.time_budget_ms` 60,000 and `bounds.max_query_bp` 2,000 on every explicit-label request, as the service sends them, so that the direct access paths and the MCP access path ask the same question; a discovery names `max_query_bp` 500 and no budget. The scenarios that vary a bound on purpose: the two stops of R-budget (480 and 420 ms, no request bound), their twins R-twin-0002 to -0005 and the 10,001 bp edge R-edge-0003 (the 60,000 ms budget alone), R-edge-0004 (a request bound of 100 bp), R-edge-0012 (no bounds) and the budget edges R-edge-0020, -0021 and -0024 (250, 70,000 and 400 ms). | the 10 kb stops of R-budget run up to the server's limit of 10,000 bp and reach the host on the direct access paths only. R-pos, R-multi, R-junction, R-trace, R-rc, R-order, R-twin-case and most of R-edge name `bounds.time_budget_ms` 20,000 and `bounds.max_query_bp` 2,000 on every explicit-label request, as the service sends them, so that the direct access paths and the MCP access path ask the same question; a discovery names `max_query_bp` 500 and no budget. The scenarios that vary a bound on purpose: the two stops of R-budget (3,000 and 8,000 ms, no request bound), their twins R-twin-0002 to -0005 (the full 10 kb and its second half) and the 10,001 bp edge R-edge-0003 (the 20,000 ms budget alone), R-edge-0004 (a request bound of 100 bp), R-edge-0012 (no bounds) and the budget edges R-edge-0020, -0021 and -0024 (250, 70,000 and 400 ms).]]

Via MCP a resolve is the `traverse_resolve` tool, a job the service runs in its queue (case `resolve.job_path`): the tool waits inline up to 30 s with explicit labels and 10 s for a discovery, else hands back a job the runner polls; the service's own deadline for the host call is the budget plus the reserve plus an allowance of 10,000 ms ([[manifest_version = 5 ? 70.25 | 30.25]] s here), and a call it ends there is a `resolve_timeout`, read as a host state when the service's timing shows the deadline was reached. The service validates first and in its own terms: it always sends its own `bounds.max_query_bp` (2,000; 500 for a discovery) and refuses a longer query at submit, so [[manifest_version = 5 ? the stops of R-budget and their twins (2,500 to 10,000 bp) | the 10 kb scenarios]] cannot be expressed; it de-duplicates labels, upper-cases the sequence, and refuses any character outside ACGT, more than 1,000 distinct labels, a budget below 500 ms or above the host's cap, and a discovery limit outside [[manifest_version = 5 ? 1 to 1,000 | 1..100]]; support, select and graph have no argument. The MCP column therefore holds many by-design and not-exercised cells; each carries its reason in one line, and appendix B names every case with the service's code and text.

R-pos.title: positive windows
R-pos.prose: Windows of 31, 32, 50, 100, 200, 1,000 and 2,000 bp cut from the records, resolved under the record's own taxid column and under its header label. The property is the simplest claim /resolve makes and the ground every other chapter stands on: every k-mer of a window taken from a record is in the graph and supported by that record's labels, as one run covering the whole query (`resolve_runs`, full), and `graph_runs` is that same single run (`resolve_graph_runs`). The lengths bracket the k-mer count from one (31 bp) and two (32 bp) to 1,970 (2,000 bp, the cap the service sends). The series changes the source record with the length, two records per length (A: eco 31, mtb 32, pae 50, cje 100, mge 200, ser 1,000, hvo 2,000 bp; B: buc, mpn, mja, sso, spo, scem, pfa in the same order), so the matrices are correctness controls across lengths and records, not a runtime-versus-length benchmark: latency varies substantially across records, and these controls do not isolate the effect of query length (in this run the 2,000 bp cells of the A and B matrices, hvo and pfa, on direct-local under the header: {x[R-pos-0026][dl][wall]} ({x[R-pos-0026][dl][host_word]}) against {x[R-pos-0028][dl][wall]} ({x[R-pos-0028][dl][host_word]})). Each request names the [[manifest_version = 5 ? 60,000 | 20,000]] ms budget, so a 503 deadline is allowed under load and reads inconclusive[[n_footnoted ?; in this run {n_footnoted} test{n_footnoted:s} did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}); the detail block{n_footnoted:s} follow{n_footnoted:v} the unit's table, and the exception index on the chapter page says what the exception means | ; in this run every test passed on every access path]]. The four units are the column and header halves over the two record sets.
R-pos.claim: a window cut from a record resolves fully under its taxid column and under its header at every length from one k-mer to 2,000 bp

R-multi.title: several labels
R-multi.prose: One 100 bp window per scenario resolved under three labels at once: the record's taxid column, its header, and the taxid column of a record from another kingdom. The record's two labels must support every k-mer (`resolve_runs`, full, once per label); the unrelated column must not support all of them (`label_not_full`). The second claim rests on the assumption that a random, DUST-filtered 100 bp window of one kingdom has at least one k-mer that a genome of another kingdom lacks; a window from a gene conserved across kingdoms would break it, and the truth of each scenario states so. Together with R-order this is the evidence that labels in one request are answered independently of each other.
R-multi.claim: labels in one request are answered independently of each other

R-junction.title: junctions
R-junction.prose: The concatenation of two 100 bp windows from records of different kingdoms, [[manifest_version = 5 ? resolved under both records' headers and both taxid columns. The expected runs are computed from the records, not assumed: A's header has the run [0, `a_end`), where `a_end` is 70 plus the number of B's leading bases that happen to repeat A's own continuation in its record (at most k - 1), and B's header has [`b_start`, 170), where `b_start` is 100 less the number of A's trailing bases that repeat what precedes B's window in its record. `resolve_runs` asks the headers for exactly these runs (on this basic graph a header supports the k-mers its own record holds and no others), so a header whose run reaches into the other record's k-mers is a wrong answer. A taxid column holds the column's other records too, which may carry a junction k-mer, so each column is asked for one run from its own record's side that ends inside the junction: A's column a run from 0 ending in [`a_end`, 100], B's a run to the end starting in [70, `b_start`], and at most 100 supported k-mers each; that the columns hold no k-mer of the other genome, another kingdom's, is the index's answer rather than a derivation from the records (tag index-empirical, the manifest's `index_empirical`). | resolved under both taxid columns. The expected runs are reference-record expectations: computed from the two records, not assumed, and holding under one stated assumption about the columns' content. A taxid column gathers every record of the taxon, and a junction k-mer that another record of the same column happens to hold would move that column's run end; the builder does not model the columns' other records, so the reference windows are not an inventory of a column's k-mers. Under that assumption A's column has the run [0, `a_end`), where `a_end` is 70 plus the number of B's leading bases that happen to repeat A's own continuation in its record (at most k - 1), and B's column has [`b_start`, 170), where `b_start` is 100 less the number of A's trailing bases that repeat what precedes B's window in its record; `resolve_runs` asks for exactly these runs (k-mer-start intervals over the 170 k-mers of the junction). A run reaching into the other record's k-mers is a mismatch to this oracle; it is a host defect only once another record of the column has been checked for the junction k-mer. [[direct_all_pass ? In this run every junction resolved as expected on both direct access paths, so the question did not arise. | In this run {n_footnoted:word} junction{n_footnoted:s} did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids}): a longer run there is read against this oracle, and whether another record of the column supports the junction k-mer is to be checked before it is attributed to the host.]]]] The {n_tests:word} junctions of this manifest expect {expected_runs_text}[[manifest_version = 5 ?, the headers' runs]].
R-junction.claim: a junction's runs end where the reference records say[[manifest_version = 5 ?: the headers' exactly, the columns' within the junction |, under the stated assumption that no other record of the column holds a junction k-mer]]

R-discover.title: discovery
R-discover.prose: A 100 bp window from a record with few relatives in RefSeq (a low-carrier genome: buc, mge, mpn, ser, mja, sso) resolved without labels, discovering column labels or header labels with `max_labels` [[manifest_version = 5 ? 9, 3, 20 or 100 | 1, 20 or 100]] (`bounds.max_query_bp` 500 and no time budget, as the service sends a discovery; a discovery reads every in-graph k-mer's whole row). [[manifest_version = 5 ? The two limits that were 1 in manifest v4 are raised to one above the ties at full support the index's earlier answers showed, eight labels on buc's window and two on ser's (the manifest's `discover_v4` and `index_empirical`), so that the source must be listed rather than allowed to hide in a tie.]] The property (`resolve_discover_contains`) accepts two kinds of evidence, and the check's detail says which it met: the source record's own label, its taxid column or its accession.version, is listed (the source observed); or the source is absent from a truncated list whose truncation statistics are compatible with an unobserved tie at full support (the source not recovered). The second kind validates the consistency of the reported ranking and truncation, not the recovery of the source, and the identities of the omitted labels are not in the answer. The source supports every in-graph k-mer of the query, so a truncated list may leave it out only in a tie at that full support, which the check verifies from `labels_truncated` (the least support kept and the most support dropped both equal to the in-graph k-mer count, at least one dropped label at full length), the ranking being all the answer can show: the tie is decided by column id, then sequence id, which the answer does not state. The invariants also require the list ranked by support, at most `max_labels` long and `labels_truncated` consistent with it. [[manifest_version = 5 ? A tie at full support can still leave the source out of a truncated list, which passes, as SPEC section 4.2's tie rule says, and the check's detail states which of the two happened | With `max_labels` 1 a tie at full support can leave the source out, which passes, as SPEC section 4.2's tie rule says]][[x[R-discover-0001][dl][pass] ? (R-discover-0001 in this run: the check's detail on direct-local, which says which of the two kinds of evidence it is, reads: {x[R-discover-0001][dl][detail]}) | ; in this run R-discover-0001 on direct-local was {x[R-discover-0001][dl][phrase]}]].
R-discover.claim: a discovery lists the source or states a truncation that SPEC section 4.2 allows

R-trace.title: trace support
R-trace.prose: 200 bp of a record resolved under its header with support trace: beyond presence, consecutive supported k-mers must have consecutive coordinates in that sequence (SPEC section 4.2), so a window cut from the record is exactly one contiguous run over every k-mer (`resolve_runs`, full). This is the chapter's only evidence of a contiguous occurrence in one record (I.1's result units); a full resolve without trace shows label support alone. The three records, E. coli, S. aureus and phage lambda, differ in the size of their column and in the number of records it holds. Not exercised via MCP: the `traverse_resolve` tool has no support argument (see B)[[n_cold_dl ?; the direct-local executions are host-cold for that reason (no MCP call reached the host before them; {n_cold_dl} of {n_tests} in this run) and the aggregate says so]].
R-trace.claim: support trace gives one contiguous run

R-budget.title: the time budget
R-budget.prose: [[manifest_version = 5 ? 5,000 bp of E. coli under 480 ms and 10,000 bp of P. aeruginosa under 420 ms (windows drawn without the uniqueness requirement and with the DUST threshold raised to 5; eco's query is the second half of such a 10 kb window), each run right after its complete twin, the same query under the 60,000 ms budget the service sends (R-twin-0002 and -0004: warm-ups the build places first, the manifest's `warms`). Each budget is chosen so that the work deadline, the budget less the 250 ms reserve, falls inside the warm work: at 230 and 170 ms, in a row batch (64 rows, assumed to double up to 4,096) that ends before the budget at the warm rate the manifest's `stop_design` was read from, which holds for warm totals of about 0.28 to 2.48 s for eco's query and 0.21 to 21.8 s for pae's, provided the k-mer lookup, which the deadline does not poll, ends within the work deadline. Whether a stop happens still depends on the batch times, so on the load and on what is warm. | 10 kb of a record (E. coli under 3,000 ms, P. aeruginosa under 8,000 ms; windows drawn without the uniqueness requirement and with the DUST threshold raised to 5) under a budget chosen so that the work stops inside the query on a cold or loaded host and completes on a warm one.]] The property is the stated stop of SPEC section 4.5: the answer is the resolve of a prefix, its stop block consistent (`num_kmers` equal to `resolved_kmers`, `resolved_bp` and `remainder_from_bp` derived from it, the stop at or after the budget less the reserve), and the record's own label supports every k-mer of that prefix as one run (`resolve_runs`, full with `prefix_if_stopped`). A complete answer never exercised the property and reads inconclusive; a 503 deadline is allowed and reads inconclusive, or a finding when it comes more than max(1 s, the budget) late on the client's clock (`budget_respected`, appendix A's decision table; where the time of a late 503 went is not isolated by that measurement). [[manifest_version = 5 ? The complete twin of each stop, the same query under 60,000 ms (R-twin-0002 and -0004, full unless stopped, run before the stop), is what the `prefix_equals` relations compare the stop against (REL-prefix_equals-0001 and -0003), and the continuation from the middle base, 2,500 for eco and 5,000 for pae (R-twin-0003 and -0005), is compared with the complete twin over the k-mers from that base (REL-prefix_equals-0002 and -0004) | The full twin of each stop, the same 10 kb under 20,000 ms (R-twin-0002 and -0004, full unless stopped), is what the `prefix_equals` relations compare the stop against (REL-prefix_equals-0001 and -0003), and the query's second half from base 5,000 (R-twin-0003 and -0005) is compared with the full twin over the k-mers from that base (REL-prefix_equals-0002 and -0004)]]: on their common k-mers the graph runs and the label's runs must be the same sets. [[manifest_version = 5 ? [[n_warm_up_direct_pairs ? [[warm_ups_all_before_target_direct ? Each complete twin's first execution in this run started before its stop's on each direct access path that ran both ({n_warm_up_direct_pairs} pairs of twin and access path compared[[mcp_all_refused_before_host ?; via MCP neither reached the host]]), as the design needs. | In this run [[n_warm_ups_after_target_direct = 1 ? one execution of a complete twin did not start before its stop's on a direct access path | {n_warm_ups_after_target_direct:word} executions of the complete twins did not start before their stops' on {warm_ups_after_target_direct_arms}]] ({warm_ups_after_target_direct_text}), against the design.]] | In this run no direct access path ran a complete twin and its stop both.]]]] In this run[[logan_caveat ?, on this host under the Logan load]], [[n_footnoted ? [[n_tests = 1 ? the only test | {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests]] did not pass on every access path ({footnoted_ids})[[footnoted_all_late503 ?: the coverage gap on the chapter page reads [[n_footnoted = 1 ? its | their]] 503 deadline{n_late503:s} past the budget and | [[n_late503 ?: the coverage gap on the chapter page reads the 503 deadline{n_late503:s} past the budget{n_late503_tests:s} of {late503_ids_text}, and | ;]]]] [[n_footnoted = 1 ? its detail block follows | their detail blocks follow]] the table[[n_clean ?; the {n_clean:word} other{n_clean:s} passed on every access path exercised: {clean_ids}]] | every test passed on every access path exercised: {members}]]. [[stop_observed ? A stated stop was answered ({stop_observed_text}). | The stated stop has not been observed on this host, so the prefix property reads inconclusive wherever it was asked.]] [[n_relations ? Of the {n_relations:word} relations, {relations_text}.]] [[n_declared_relations ? The deploy gate's declared file excludes {declared_relations_text}, with the owner's reasons in appendix G.]] [[mcp_all_refused_before_host ? Not exercised via MCP: [[manifest_version = 5 ? every query exceeds the service's supported length of 2,000 bp and the stops' budgets lie below its minimum of 500 ms | the query exceeds the service's supported length of 2,000 bp]], so every call was refused at submit (see B). | Via MCP: {mcp_classes_text} (see B).]]
R-budget.claim: [[manifest_version = 5 ? a resolve under a budget inside its warm work, run right after its complete twin, answers a stated prefix that its complete twin agrees with | a 10 kb resolve under a small budget answers a stated prefix that its full twin agrees with]]

R-edge.title: edge inputs
R-edge.prose: The edges of /resolve's validation and of its alphabet, one input each, on 100 bp of E. coli unless the edge is the length (the [[manifest_version = 5 ? three discovery edges, R-edge-0022, -0023 and -0025, | two discovery edges, R-edge-0022 and -0023,]] take its first 60 bp). Refused inputs expect the host's exact 400 text, or its prefix where the text carries a value: k - 1 bases, 10,001 bp (above the server's limit of 10,000), 200 bp against a request bound of 100, an unknown label (named), a duplicate label (refused, not merged, as the source decides), an empty sequence, discover together with labels and neither of the two, an unknown field (named), graph and graphs on a single-graph server, a body that is not an object and one that is not JSON, a budget not above the 250 ms reserve, and `discover.max_labels` 0. Accepted inputs expect a 200 with the right profile: exactly k bases (one k-mer, `graph_runs` [[0, 1]]); an N or an IUPAC R at position 50, which /resolve does not refuse, the 31 k-mers holding it being absent from the graph (`graph_runs` [[0, 20], [51, 70]]) and the label supporting the 39 others; lower case, resolved as upper case; 1,001 explicit labels, which the host does not cap; a random 200 bp with no k-mer in the graph (`resolve_absent`[[manifest_version = 5 ?, its chance of a graph k-mer bounded in the manifest's truth, `chance_bound`]]); a budget of 70,000 ms lowered to the server's 60,000 and stated (clamped); [[manifest_version = 5 ? `discover.max_labels` 150, within the service's discovery cap of 1,000 (100 at the v4 run), so expected answered on every access path with eco's column listed or in a tie at full support (`resolve_discover_contains`); and the two split cases the service refuses but the host answers, `discover.max_labels` 1,001 (above the cap) and a budget of 400 ms. | and the two split cases the service refuses but the host answers, `discover.max_labels` 150 and a budget of 400 ms.]] The texts of the refusals were read from the source where no smoke run had exercised them (tag code-derived). The expectation column is the host's; via MCP most of the family is decided by the service, in four ways the tables state per row with the service's status and code (the counts and the inputs here come from the same classifier as the cells): not expressible through MCP ({n_mcp_not_expressible} input{n_mcp_not_expressible:s}, no call made: {mcp_not_expressible_variants}); refused before host execution ({n_mcp_refused_before_host} input{n_mcp_refused_before_host:s} the service's own validation or its route refuses at submit: {mcp_refused_before_host_variants}[[x[R-edge-0003][mcp][class] = refused_before_host ?; the 10,001 bp query it refuses at its own 2,000 bp before the host's limit applies, so that input reads not exercised like the not-expressible ones]]); the host's refusal relayed through the service under its own code ({n_mcp_relayed}: {mcp_relayed_variants}); and answered after service normalisation ({n_mcp_normalised}: {mcp_normalised_variants}[[x[R-edge-0009][mcp][class] = normalised ?, the duplicate labels de-duplicated, so the host answers 200 where the direct request is refused]]). [[x[R-edge-0007][mcp][class] = answered ? The lower case of R-edge-0007 is upper-cased by the service too, but the host answers it as sent, so that pair is one of the {n_mcp_answered} the host answered through the service, agreeing with the direct access paths.]] [[n_mcp_by_design ? The {n_mcp_by_design} pair{n_mcp_by_design:s} standing by design are cases appendix B names[[mcp_by_design_all_verified ?, every one verified by the comparison | ({n_mcp_by_design_verified} verified, {n_mcp_by_design_unverified} not)]]; the | The]] {n_mcp_not_exercised} not exercised have no MCP answer to compare.
R-edge.claim: every refusal carries the host's exact text and every accepted edge the right profile, the budget above the cap lowered and stated, the budget at the reserve refused

R-rc.title: reverse complement
R-rc.prose: [[manifest_version = 5 ? The reverse complement of a 100 bp window none of whose reverse k-mers its record holds, the whole record searched k-mer by k-mer (S. aureus, E. coli; eco takes the place of v4's M. jannaschii, whose window's reverse complement was absent from the graph altogether, a plain absence that says nothing of the strand), resolved under the record's header. | The reverse complement of a 100 bp window that occurs once on either strand of its record (S. aureus, M. jannaschii), resolved under the record's header.]] On this basic graph a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes and the index holds the records' forward strands, so the header supports none of the query's k-mers: `kmers_supported` 0, the label still listed (`resolve_runs` with kmers 0). [[manifest_version = 5 ? The premise that zero needs is k-mer-level, no k-mer of the reverse complement on the record's forward strand, and the builder verified it when choosing the windows. The check tells the strands apart only where the reverse k-mers are in the graph through other records; the manifest records the evidence behind the choice of windows (`reverse_in_graph_evidence`: sau's reverse complement in the graph whole in earlier runs, eco's many RefSeq records), and the check does not ask. | The premise that zero needs is k-mer-level: no k-mer of the reverse complement may lie on the record's forward strand, that is, no k-mer of the window may recur on the record's reverse strand. The v4 builder chose each window as it chooses the positive windows, occurring once on either strand of its record, and did not search the record for the reverse complement's k-mers one by one; the uniqueness of a 100 bp window does not imply the uniqueness of each of its 31-mers, so the premise was not established by the builder. The pass shows that the index answered 0 for these two windows, as expected; it does not verify the premise independently of the index (manifest v5 does, when choosing the windows). Whether the reverse k-mers are in the graph at all, through other genomes, the check does not ask, so a zero here cannot tell a strand-specific absence from a plain absence of those k-mers from the graph.]] This is the resolve-side statement of the strand fact that chapters P, T (T-strand, whose seed window is chosen so that none of its reverse k-mers is in the record) and N test on their routes.
R-rc.claim: a reverse complement is another query on this forward-strand graph

R-order.title: label order
R-order.prose: The labels of an R-multi request in another order (header, unrelated column, taxid) on a 100 bp window of H. volcanii: the taxid column and the header support every k-mer as when they are named first. `resolve_runs` reads a label by its name, so the check is order-blind by construction; the scenario tests that the host is too.
R-order.claim: labels are answered independently of their order

R-twin.title: twins
R-twin.prose: The upper-case twin of the lower-case resolve R-edge-0007: the same 100 bp of E. coli in upper case, expected full under the column, and the relation `same_answer`, which requires the two bodies to be equal apart from timing, on every access path (via MCP the service upper-cases the lower-case request before the host sees it[[rel[REL-same_answer-0003][mcp] = pass ?, so the two answers are the same there too | ; in this run the relation reads {rel[REL-same_answer-0003][mcp]} there]]). The other twins made for relations, the [[manifest_version = 5 ? complete and the continued resolves of R-budget's queries | full and the continued 10 kb resolves]], are printed with R-budget, whose relations they serve.
R-twin.claim: the upper-case twin answers byte for byte like the lower-case resolve

R-warm.title: warm-ups
R-warm.prose: Eight resolves that warm the rows a scenario of another chapter reads, each placed right before its target (the manifest's `warms`; build_manifest.place_warm_ups), so that the target's first execution, the MCP access path's cold call, meets rows the host has just read: a manifest choice after the v4 run's cold first calls, which the document states beside the target's time without attributing that time to it. Five read, under the record's header, the seed of a multi-copy repeat walk and the record's continuation as far as the walk's minimum reaches on each requested traversal arm (direction) plus a margin, within its radius (areas.py `minimum_warm_up`): one each for T-repeat-0001, -0003 and -0004 (R-warm-0001, -0003 and -0004) and two for T-repeat-0002, the seed with its left extent (R-warm-0002) and the seed's last k - 1 bases with its right extent (R-warm-0008), each under its own budget. R-warm-0005 reads the region of T-labels-0003's walk under eco's taxid column, R-warm-0007 the region of T-walk-0009's walk under lambda's single-record column, and R-warm-0006 the telomeric k-mers of N-hard-0022's seed, `(TTAGGG)^10`, under the human column, whose support is the index's answer in earlier runs rather than a record's (tag index-empirical). Each is a positive resolve in its own right, 60 to 743 bp under a label its target walks under (a record's header for the five repeat warm-ups, a taxid column for the three others) with the 60,000 ms budget and the 2,000 bp bound the service sends, so the MCP access path sends it too: every k-mer supported as one run (`resolve_runs`, full) within the budget (`budget_respected`). [[n_warm_up_arm_pairs ? [[warm_ups_all_before_target ?
